meta.title: Lacuna UX map
meta.userRequestModel: Every action is written as: the user wants X; the user needs to do X; intuitivity = 1-10.
meta.sourcePolicy: Code and executable tests are authoritative. Product documentation was not used to assert current behaviour.
meta.obsoleteCatalogue: docs/APP-FLOWS.md was deleted before replacement artefacts were created and is not an evidence source.
meta.noteOnScores: Scores are heuristic source-audit judgements, not observed usability measurements.
meta.mapReading: Current stations are semantic control clusters. Repeated JSX instances are represented by occurrenceRefs rather than pretending every rendered row is a unique concept.

deliveryOverlay.basis: Implementation source inspection, a consolidated desktop and narrow-width browser walkthrough, focused regression tests, merge-base red-to-green proof, static checks, the production build, the full unit suite and the web end-to-end suite. The 2026-08-29 audit stations, actions, observations and heuristic scores remain an unchanged historical snapshot.

statusMeaning.delivered: The implemented source covers the recommendation's agreed scope.
statusMeaning.partially delivered: A bounded part of the recommendation is implemented; the remaining scope is named explicitly.
statusMeaning.not addressed: No delivery was included in this change.

anchors.1: Unusable or effectively unreachable in the audited surface.
anchors.10: Directly labelled, expected location, immediate result, low-risk and reversible.
anchors.8-9: Clear and predictable with one minor branch or context dependency.
anchors.6-7: Works once discovered but competes with nearby concepts, hides detail or needs a mode/menu.
anchors.4-5: Requires translation, advanced knowledge, or carries meaningful ambiguity/risk.
anchors.2-3: Redirect, legacy language, contradictory destination or largely invisible operation.

specialStatuses.confirmed: Rendered or routed in production source.
specialStatuses.legacy: Still reachable for compatibility, not a current destination.
specialStatuses.contradictory: Rendered behaviour and user expectation disagree, or duplicate controls compete.
specialStatuses.implied: A reasonable user expectation is not represented as a rendered control; score is null.
specialStatuses.dead: No live control established; retained as an audit finding rather than a fabricated score.

coverage.jsxInteractionCountNote: 842 is a static AST count of interaction-bearing production TSX nodes, including repeated component instances and motion/container handlers. It is not a count of unique user concepts.

recommendations.title: Make Study the single primary learning entry point
recommendations.currentFriction: Study, Practice Now, Review today, due review, course progression and question practice are all valid but appear as competing labels or separate routes.
recommendations.proposedChange: Keep Study as the only generic course action. Put due review, progression, assessment revision, practice scope and session modes inside one chooser. Keep Review today as the explicit global scope.
recommendations.rationale: The source already has a course conductor; the problem is the number of visible doors into it.

recommendations.title: Replace Read/Edit duplication with one explicit authoring mode
recommendations.currentFriction: Read/Edit appears on the path, lesson and course settings; inline rename and settings rename duplicate each other.
recommendations.proposedChange: Make Author mode a course/lesson workspace state, keep the toolbar toggle near the content, and remove the duplicate default from Course settings except for a global preference.
recommendations.rationale: The code already gates controls by mode; the map exposes the duplicate choice.

delivery.scope: Course paths and lesson views now share one Study/Author workspace mode beside the content, and Course settings no longer repeats the mode control.

recommendations.title: Create one data centre organised by job
recommendations.currentFriction: Share, import, full backup, card export, merge updates and sync overlap in payload language but sit in unrelated pages.
recommendations.proposedChange: Use one Data area with Add/import, Share/publish, Backup/restore and Sync as clear jobs; preserve security copy and route old links to the right job.
recommendations.rationale: Users think in what they want to move, not in which serialization implementation produced it.

recommendations.title: Use one Add content control
recommendations.currentFriction: Card, sequence, occlusion, import and link-existing actions are repeated at page, lesson and menu level.
recommendations.proposedChange: Keep one Add content control whose first decision is Card, Sequence, Occlusion, Question or Import/link; retain contextual shortcuts only where they are genuinely faster.
recommendations.rationale: The current system has multiple entry points to the same authoring families.

delivery.scope: The Cards library now presents Card, Sequence and Occlusion creation as one labelled Add content group and no longer repeats a second empty-state action cluster. Question, import/link and lesson-level entry points remain separate.

recommendations.title: Make questions path-native and reuse the study vocabulary
recommendations.currentFriction: Question work is structurally separate from the Card-based course conductor, despite sharing lessons, concepts and assessment intent.
recommendations.proposedChange: Expose Questions as an assessment content type on the course path and share response, feedback, correction and finish language with card study.
recommendations.rationale: The router comments explicitly describe question practice as deliberately separate while evidence is validated; that is a product seam, not a user mental model.

recommendations.title: Turn settings into task groups
recommendations.currentFriction: Settings is a long section rail mixing appearance, input, dashboard, study, scheduler, course policy, sync, AI, install and backups.
recommendations.proposedChange: Group settings under Appearance and access, Study behaviour, Course defaults, Data safety and Integrations. Put advanced scheduler controls behind a deliberate disclosure.
recommendations.rationale: The source's section list is already an unambiguous information-architecture inventory.

delivery.scope: Global settings are grouped under Appearance and access, Study behaviour, Course defaults, Data safety and Integrations while existing child section anchors remain available for direct links.

recommendations.title: Remove legacy deck language and repair onboarding import links
recommendations.currentFriction: Welcome sends Import Anki / JSON and Import a deck to /settings; legacy deck/bank routes remain as redirects.
recommendations.proposedChange: Route onboarding import links to the actual import job, use course/card terminology everywhere current, and retain redirects only for old bookmarks.
recommendations.rationale: This is a source-confirmed contradiction, not a usability opinion.

delivery.scope: Both Welcome links use current course terminology and open /share with an explicit import intent; the Share page scrolls to and focuses its existing import job, and compatibility redirects remain for old bookmarks. Current-facing deck terminology remains in course scheduling guidance, the duplicate-card warning and the legacy import preview.

recommendations.title: Clarify quick commands versus full search
recommendations.currentFriction: Sidebar Search opens a command palette, while /search is a separate content-search page and both compete for the same label.
recommendations.proposedChange: Label the palette Quick actions and the page Search content, or merge them behind one Search surface with command mode as a tab.
recommendations.rationale: The two controls have different jobs but the same noun.

delivery.scope: The keyboard overlay and its sidebar trigger are now Quick search; the routed library surface and sidebar fallback are Search content, with matching shortcut copy.

recommendations.title: Make assessment and practice planning path-native
recommendations.currentFriction: Checkpoint authoring, practice-node authoring, unlock policy and revision plans are split between path and settings.
recommendations.proposedChange: Create and edit checkpoints/practice nodes from the path; keep detailed coverage and scheduling as progressive detail in the same task.
recommendations.rationale: The path already renders the resulting objects; creation should happen where users see them.

delivery.scope: Author mode can create and edit practice nodes and checkpoints directly from the course path, including assessment date, placement, coverage and exclusions through the shared editor. Unlock policy remains in Course Settings, while revision planning remains in the assessment study flow.

recommendations.title: Expose one data-safety contract
recommendations.currentFriction: Merge, replace, sync, channel deletion, MCP destructive access and browser persistence all change data safety with different copy and confirmations.
recommendations.proposedChange: Use shared language for snapshot, scope, recovery, irreversible impact and undo; show a common safety preview before commit.
recommendations.rationale: The code contains safety primitives but not one user-facing contract.

delivery.scope: Restore-point deletion now names the local scope and states that mirrored files are retained. The wider shared safety preview across merge, replace, sync, channel and MCP operations is not implemented.

recommendations.title: Make AI trust boundaries one first-class flow
recommendations.currentFriction: Web AI, terminal AI, batch prompting, memory inspection and MCP grants look related but use different entry points and different consent semantics.
recommendations.proposedChange: Use an Integrations area that clearly separates web relay, Electron terminal and MCP; explain what leaves the device, what is remembered and how access ends.
recommendations.rationale: The code deliberately separates the transports; the UI should make that separation legible.

recommendations.title: Standardise destructive confirmation, restore and undo
recommendations.currentFriction: Some destructive actions use ConfirmInline, some rely on hidden context menus, some expose undo only through a toast, and some are irreversible.
recommendations.proposedChange: Use one confirmation contract with impact, scope, recovery path and a consistent Undo where technically safe.
recommendations.rationale: The product already has confirmation and undo implementations; they need one behavioural contract.

delivery.scope: Restore-point deletion now uses an explicit inline confirmation with impact and recovery-boundary copy, and keeps the confirmation open when deletion fails. Other destructive flows retain their existing contracts.

recommendations.title: Hide scheduler internals behind progressive disclosure
recommendations.currentFriction: Retention, interval fuzz, steps, leeches, optimisation and practice thresholds expose many low-level decisions before a learner knows whether they need them.
recommendations.proposedChange: Lead with workload, goal and study behaviour. Put scheduler internals under Advanced scheduling with plain-language summaries and a reset path.
recommendations.rationale: The current controls are individually labelled but collectively impose a translation burden.

delivery.scope: Workload and session goals remain visible while interval, learning-step and leech controls, practice thresholds and scheduling optimisation sit behind deliberate disclosures with plain-language summaries and a reset path.

recommendations.title: Give installation and update state a visible home
recommendations.currentFriction: PWA install availability and Electron auto-update outcomes are conditional or invisible.
recommendations.proposedChange: Show installation status, current version, update state, retry and release notes where the environment supports them.
recommendations.rationale: The updater is a real background operation with no user-facing control or result.

deadLegacyImplied.title: Browser permission recovery
deadLegacyImplied.userExpectation: If camera, storage or clipboard permission is denied, the app explains how to recover.
deadLegacyImplied.currentReality: The browser owns the prompt; source audit finds actions and fallbacks but no single permission centre.

deadLegacyImplied.title: No confidently dead rendered control established
deadLegacyImplied.userExpectation: A visible control should lead somewhere.
deadLegacyImplied.currentReality: Static source audit identified redirects, contradictions and implied gaps, but did not establish a rendered JSX control that is unreachable in production.
deadLegacyImplied.note: Do not invent a dead-control score without runtime reachability evidence.

auditNotes: Static source audit deliberately excludes browser validation; camera, clipboard, file picker, directory picker, storage persistence and PWA install are included as boundary actions rather than verified outcomes.
Electron is first-class in the map: titlebar, updater, MCP companion, per-scope grants, consent prompts, disconnect semantics and undo are included.
The old APP-FLOWS catalogue was not carried forward as truth. Where its links or wording would have conflicted, this map uses current source paths and route definitions.
No confidently dead rendered JSX control was established from source alone. Redirects and missing/implied affordances are listed explicitly instead.
Recommendations are not implementation instructions. They are product changes to evaluate, with affected stations, effort, dependencies and expected intuition movement.
